COMPONENTS

The vehicle is equipped with:

  • a function that automatically switches on the dipped headlamps when light conditions are poor.
  • the function known as Parking (follow me home) keeps the exterior lights on for a timed period after the ignition key has been removed. If the light is below 850 LUX, the dipped headlamps remain on for 45 seconds.
  • after having turned the ignition OFF, a flash switches on the dipped headlamps for 1 minute. It is possible to interrupt this by operating the headlamp flasher switch again (this function does not control the buzzer for lights remaining on when the doors are opened).
  • A funciton for automatically switching on the direction indicators in the case of strong deceleration or an impact with the activation of a two tone horn.

The direction indicators are located:

  • in the door mirrors,
  • in the front and rear light clusters.

The rear light clusters include:

  • the direction indicators,
  • the brake lights, the 3rd brake light is located at the top of the tailgate,
  • the reversing lights,
  • the rear fog lamps.

The interior lighting is ensured by the management of the following equipment:

  • one courtesy light in the 1st row,
  • one courtesy light in the 2nd row,
  • one courtesy light in the 3rd row,
  • one light in the driver and passenger sun visor,
  • one light in the glove compartment,
  • one light in the driver's front door,
  • one light in the passenger front door,
  • two lights in the luggage compartment.

The switching on and off of the courtesy lights takes place gradually (variation in the voltage at the bulb terminals), unless they are switched on manually. The map reading lights in the front courtesy light, the lights in the luggage compartment, glove compartment, vanity mirrors and front doors do not switch on and off gradually.

The switching on of the interior lighting is activated by:

  • pressing the centrally operated switch (front courtesy light console),
  • opening one of the four doors or the boot,
  • extracting the ignition key within a minute of a break in the +ACC,
  • unlocking the doors (if the key is not in the anti-theft function position and is in position +ACC),
  • vehicle location function.

The switching off of the interior lighting is activated by:

  • moving the central control switch to the "forced switching off" position
  • closing the door
  • locking/superlocking the vehicle
  • inserting the key for starting the engine (moving from +ACC to +APC).

The courtesy light function is divided into three states:

  • Rest state: courtesy light function off.
  • Brief lighting: lighting timed for a period of 30 seconds.
  • Long lighting: lighting timed for a period of 10 minutes.

The courtesy light switches on gradually over a period of 1 second.

It switches off gradually in 4 seconds.

All the lights operate with a delay timer to prevent the battery being run down.

Courtesy light lighting when the key is extracted from the ignition:

The detection of the presence of the key is activated for 1 minute after the +ACC interruption.

When this timed period has elapsed, the lighting function when the key is extracted is no longer activated.

The boot lighting function: is guaranteed by two 5W bulbs, controlled by the NBC depending on the position of the three position switch and the status of the doors.

The vanity mirror lighting function: is guaranteed by 1 component fitted with 2 x 2W bulbs, the bulbs light up when the sun visors containing the vanity mirrors are opened and the ignition is in the "ACC" or "MAR" position.

The glove compartment lighting function: is guaranteed by a 5W bulb with the ignition in the "ACC" or "MAR" position.

The front door lighting function: is guaranteed by two 5W bulbs.

Operation

The courtesy lights are controlled by a three position switch:

  • automatic switching on,
  • constantly on,
  • permanently off.

Front and rear courtesy lights function

The NBC acquires the command for the button and manages the operation of the courtesy light.

For the management of the automatic switching on of the courtesy light, the NBC uses information relating to the status of the doors (produced by the door nodes), the request for locking/unlocking and the presence of the key.

Map reading lights function

Power supply is possible with the key in the +ACC position and the bulb is controlled directly by the button.

Interior equipment brightness adjustment

The NQS acquires information from the light dimmer, determines the lighting level required and then transfers the information to the NBC.

The NBC knows the status of the lights (day/night).

The NBC controls the switching on of the lights indicating the position of the following (with no dimmer function):

  • ashtray,
  • door switches,
  • seat switches,
  • various buttons.

The NBC transmits information concerning the lighting level to the NQS, to the radio and to the NIT, to the NCL (Climate Control Node) and to the NSC (Multifunction Screen Node) by means of the VAN confort network for the lighting or lighting adjustment.

Ignition switch: incorporated in the steering column switch unit module.

Headlamp alignment correction motor: incorporated in the lamp.

Headlamp alignment manual correction: makes it possible to adjust the four lighting positions manually: 0, 1, 2 and 3.

The switch is located to the left of the steering wheel, at the bottom of the dashboard.

Headlamp alignment automatic correction (for xenon lamps): on vehicles fitted with xenon lamps, the automatic correction of the headlamp alignment is managed by the headlamp control units based on the signals produced by the two sensors which measure the angle of the bodyshell.

The NBC: manages the direct operation of the bulbs and the NDVM control for the power supply for the dipped headlamps, main beam headlamps and fog lights.

The solar ray sensor: is fastened to the dashborad and transmits the information detected directly to the NBC for the management of the function that automatically switches on the lights and the climate control system.

It manages the lighting and the switching off of:

  • the front and rear side lights (and the number plate light).
  • the dipped headlamps.

When the automatic switching on function is activated, the system manages the switching on and off of the lights according to:

  • the exterior light conditions (day/night)
  • the presence of a tunnel or poorly lit car park
  • area in prolonged shade (e.g. woodland)
  • the automatic windscreen wiping system.

The system does not ask for the lights to be switched on whilst driving under a bridge or in a partly shaded area.

The moment the vehicle stops, if the light conditions are very poor, the system keeps the lights on for long enough to allow the user to get out of the vehicle and do anything they may need to do.

manual controls for switching the lights on always take precendence.

Operation in fault conditions.

If there is a fault in the system, this does not cause the lights to go out inappropriately.

If the fault is detected when starting up, the function for automatically switching the lights on is immediately inhibited and the driver is advised of this.

No type of fault in the automatic light management system has any effect on the manual operation.

The system does not take into account the colour of the windscreen.

Supply circuit: The sensor receives a +5V power supply and the system does not have a fuse.

The solar ray sensor contains the following sensors:

  • Twilight sensor - a sensor that sends information concerning the outside light conditions
  • Tunner sensor - a sensor that sends information concerning the light level in front of the vehicle.

Electrical output signals:

  • Twighlight (used for the automatic function for switching on the lights)
  • Tunnel (used for the automatic function for switching on the lights)
  • Solar (used for the climate control system)

Automatic switching on of lights

The aim of this function is to automatically control the switching on and off of the lighting system depending on the outside light conditions or the operation of the windscreen wiper system.

The level for switching on the lights corresponds to the moment when 30% of drivers would have activated the control on a vehicle not equipped with this automatic function.

The level for switching off the lights corresponds to the moment when 70% of drivers would have switched the lights off.

After switching off the engine, the lights remain on if the exterior light conditions dictate.

The detection parameters make it possible to distinguish between day and night, driving under a bridge, in a tunnel or in a poorly lit car park.

The system comprises the following components:

  • a brightness sensor fitted on the dashboard.
  • the NBC.

OPERATING PRINCIPLES

The automatic switching on function is only activated or deactivated with the key in the +ACC position by pressing the button at the end of the left steering column switch unit lever for at least 2 seconds.

An auditory warning produced by the NVO plus a message on the multifuction screen accompany the activation and deactivation of the automatic lighting function.

The manual control for switching on the side lights is only signalled by a pictogram.

The brightness information produced by the solar ray sensor is received directly by the NBC.

The intermittent, low speed, high speed and AUTO screen washing functions are activated after an automatic timed switching on.

The timed period is:

  • 40 seconds for intermittent operation
  • 10 seconds for the low speed
  • 2 seconds for the high speed

The automatic interruption of the lighting is controlled 15 seconds after the screen washing function has stopped.

Switching on of reversing light

The switch is supplied with the key in the ON position; the NBC acquires control information and supplies the bulbs directly. This information is also sent via the VAN CONFORT network.

Automatic switching on of hazard warning lights

INTRODUCTION

The aim of this function is to improve safety whilst driving in traffic, automatically signalling sudden deceleration by switching the hazard warning lights on.

The lights can also be switched off automatically, depending on the vehicle parameters.

Automatic operation takes precedence over manual controls.

OPERATING PRINCIPLE

The system continuously measures vehicle acceleration when the engine is running. If this is below - 7m/s2 and the speed is above 40 km/h, the hazard warning lights are switched on automatically.

The lights are switched off automatically:

  • automatically when the vehicle acceleration becomes decidedly positive,
  • manually by pressing the hazard warning lights on/off button located at the bottom of the dashboard to the left of the steering wheel.

the automatic switching off mode is only possible if the switching on was in the automatic mode.

Switching the engine off does not have any effect on the switching off of the lights.

Switching on of danger signal

The NQS acquires the control for the hazard warning lights button and transmits it to the NBC via the VAN CONFORT network.

The NBC operates all the direction indicators directly, transmits the command to switch the direction indicator warning lights and the LED in the button on to the NQS and the command to operate the auditory warning (buzzer) to the NVO.

The operation of the button LED circuit is PWM to allow it to be lit up at night or to signal its activation.

In the case of an impact or for the management of the automatic switching on mode, the NBC uses the vehicle speed and longitudinal acceleration information via the CAN and the Air Bag Node information via the VAN CAR1 network.

Switching on of direction indicators

The NVO acquires the request to switch on the left or right direction indicator and transmits it to the NBC.

The management of the lights and the warning lights by the NBC is identical to the description for the danger signal.

The presence of a burnt out bulb produces a doubling of the frequency for switching on the lights for the direction indicator function only (2.5 Hertz instead of 1.25).

The fault diagnosis is carried out by the NBC by comparing the value of the current effectively absorbed compared with the rated value (47 W). There is no fault diagnosis for the side repeaters (5 W).

The fault diagnosis makes it possible to identify the side of the vehicle where the bulb has blown.

Ignition module and electronic module

The ignition module forms part of the control unit and is fastened to the bottom of the lamp; it consists of a casing and an independently shielded beam fitted with specific connections on the bulb side and a computer that cannot be repaired.

The ignition module releases a voltage of 1Kv at the bulb D1 terminals during the switching on stage and then it supplies an alternating voltage at 250 Hz.

The transformation of 1Kv %rarr; 25 Kv is carried out inside the bulb D1 to ensure the production of the electric arc.

Its specifications are:

  • power output: 35 watt,
  • Operating voltage: 8.5 volt - 18 volt,
  • Life: 3000 hours - 5000 hours.

Tilt sensors: these are fastened to one of the bodywork components and are connected to the front and rear suspension arms at the anti-roll bar by means of a system of connecting rods. They are designed to measure the position of the vehicle and their travel is ± 45 degrees.

The sensors provide a PWM (Pulse Width Modulation) type output voltage, i.e. a square wave signal with a frequency of 200Hz with a variable cyclical ratio. The cyclical ratio is proportional to the angle of the lever.

Do not disconnect the bulb or ignition unit when voltage is present.

Never handle any components whatsoever when voltage is present.

Never handle a hot bulb (RISK OF GAS LEAKS).
